newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat firm despite India contract controversy.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat firm despite India contract controversy.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange wheat stayed firm on Monday with November 1997 trading A$2.50 higher at A$173.00 a tonne on three lots sold.
January 1998 eased by 50 cents to A$170.00 a tonne on five lots traded.
Brokers said the controversy over Indian complaints of exotic weed found in Australian wheat shipments was having no effect on the local market.
Any effect on local markets would depend on how the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) handled the matter, they said.
Front months SFE wheat futures contract prices were being propped up by the AWB, which held all the wheat.
This left SFE wheat futures a little expensive by world standards, they said.
